analysis:
All four changed files in this batch are test-only. No production source is in the supplied evidence. I found no concrete security regression and no new attack surface in the tests themselves.

AddonHoldStoreTests.swift (head lines 36-62, 100-107): adds readFIFOWithoutWriter and AddonResultBox helpers, plus a test that a FIFO planted at addon-hold.json yields .invalid without blocking. The helper releases a blocked reader by opening the FIFO O_WRONLY and then closing it, so a failure cannot hang the test process. This covers the T-059 / TB-012 local-DoS surface, where a same-UID process plants a non-regular file at a hold-state path. It checks that AddonHoldStore.read refuses non-regular files without blocking.

AddonIPCServerTests.swift (head lines 136-177, 224-247): adds tests that unsigned silent peers cannot exhaust AddonIPCServer.maximumConnections, because the peer is authenticated at accept time rather than at the first request line. It also tests a per-request deadline for a trickled, unfinished line. These tests assert the mitigation for T-059 (unsigned same-UID program holding or starving the add-on socket). The corresponding production code in AddonIPCServer is not supplied. Whether it actually authenticates on accept, evicts or closes unauthorized peers, and enforces requestTimeout cannot be verified here.

NemotronSuperManagedSlotTests+AddonHold.swift: tests that an add-on hold unloads the Super slot while retaining the loaded-models preload plan. This relates to A-018 and does not touch the A-001 data path.

LifecycleMailboxTests.swift (head lines 70-81): tests that a FIFO in place of a mailbox request file is ignored without blocking. This is TB-003 local-operator hardening.

Remaining question for integration: the production changes these tests exercise (AddonHoldStore.read, LifecycleMailbox.readRequest, AddonIPCServer accept-time auth and request timeout) are outside this batch. Their correctness is unverified. The tests only assert intended behavior and do not prove it.
